$comment: c106 pe: stdin/stdout/stderr = MACROS -> (__acrt_iob_func(N)) (a FUNCTION import that sidesteps the D-LK-EXTERN-DATA-IMPORT pe wall; elf DATA symbols stay [elf]) + fgetws/fputws + _wfopen/_wpopen + SEEK_* (0/1/2). | Model 3 (2026-06-09): PLATFORM-NEUTRAL descriptor. `library` is a per-object-format map; the active target's format selects its runtime image at compile_pipeline resolution. The `fseek` offset (param[1]) and `ftell` result are the C `long` type, encoded here in the LP64 (i64) form correct for the runnable elf/macho targets. FC3 c1: the Windows LLP64 (i32) form for these 2 is now declared per-symbol via signatureByDataModel (the active format dataModel selects it; D-LANG-PLATFORM-DEPENDENT-PRIMITIVE-WIDTH). ★ c82 (D-FFI-SHELL-STDIO-SEMANTIC-SURFACE): (1) `typedefs` ships FILE as an opaque named struct `struct "FILE" {}` — the EXACT TypeId every signature below already spells (★ TF-C111, D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION P3: BACK to the zero-size opaque form, and the 48B interlude is RETIRED rather than ported. c109 had SIZED it to 48B = the x64 msvcrt legacy `_iobuf` for ONE reason — the msvcrt `stdout` macro was `(&__iob_func()[1])`, an INDEX into a FILE array, which needs the element STRIDE. The UCRT accessor `__acrt_iob_func(1)` returns the `FILE*` DIRECTLY, so no code in the tree indexes a FILE any more and the whole stride dependency is DELETED, not carried across. Keeping 48 would now be a LIE with a consumer waiting for it: UCRT's own FILE is `struct _iobuf { void* _Placeholder; }` = 8 bytes, so the first `sizeof(FILE)` to appear would silently read 48. Zero-size is the HONEST model — the program only ever holds `FILE*` and never materializes one; the empty field list keeps `.member` fail-loud, and it is equally honest on elf/macho, where the real records are 216B/152B and neither is 48) (interner-deduped), the dirent.json DIR precedent: `FILE *f` resolves in type position (+ the parse oracle steers block-scope `FILE *in;` declarations), member access on it fails loud. size_t rides too — C89 7.19.1 REQUIRES stdio.h to provide size_t + NULL without stddef.h (sqlite's shell.c never includes stddef.h); u64 = the stddef.json width (LP64+LLP64 agree), first-wins dedup makes double-provision with stddef/string/stdlib/time moot. (2) the printf family ships as VARIADIC externs (`fn(..., ...)`) — the c14c fcntl/ioctl mechanism; the README's variadic-exclusion note predates c14c and is updated. vfprintf's third param is spelled `va_list` — resolved by the reader's named-type bindings (threaded from the semantic tier's per-CC va_list mint, D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-VA-LIST-TYPE) so the descriptor stays arch-NEUTRAL while the param lands the ABI-exact type (SysV: __va_list_tag[1]; AAPCS64: the 32B __va_list struct; Win64: char*) — byte-identical to a user-written `extern int vfprintf(FILE*, const char*, va_list);`. (3) popen/pclose are NOT shipped: shell.c self-declares popen/pclose at file scope (goal-2: the user decl wins + FF5 binds the default libc); shipping them un-consumed would be over-ship — additive when a real consumer lands. ★ TF-C27 (D-SHIPPED-SYMBOL-PER-TARGET-AVAILABILITY, the unistd.json fdatasync/fallocate precedent): fileno IS now shipped — `int fileno(FILE*)` (glibc /usr/include/stdio.h:883) — because a real consumer landed: sqlite src/test_quota.c calls it on the POSIX path (fsync(fileno(p->f)) :15792, ftruncate(fileno(...)) :15853, fstat(fileno(...)) :15877/:15894). Gated per-symbol availableObjectFormats:[elf] — need-driven (the sole consumer is the elf testfixture) AND eager-import-safe: glibc exports it WEAK (`W fileno@@GLIBC_2.2.5` x86_64 + `W fileno@@GLIBC_2.17` arm64, nm -D libc.so.6 — present=resolvable at load, the W-is-safe rule), so both elf run legs bind it. pe + macho are DEFERRED (fail loud S0001 until a consumer lands there): on pe the C name `fileno` is `#define fileno _fileno` over msvcrt's `_fileno` export, so a bare `fileno` import would break every pe stdio binary's LOAD (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT) — the pe form needs a `_fileno` symbol + a `fileno`→`_fileno` macro (the __iob_func precedent); macho HAS fileno but has no consumer/run-witness — the stdout elf(c84)→macho(c117) staging precedent. RUN witness: examples/c-subset/shipped_fileno (fileno(stdin/stdout/stderr) == 0/1/2 → exit 42, elf x86_64 + arm64). (4) ★ c84 (D-LK-EXTERN-DATA-IMPORT, the §B-locked option A): stdout/stderr/stdin ship as extern DATA OBJECTS (`kind: object`, type FILE* — the layout engine derives the 8-byte pointer size/alignment from the DataModel, never hardcoded), gated `availableObjectFormats: ["elf"]` — the ELF exec formats declare `dataImportBinding: copy-relocation` (exec-local .bss slot + DEFINED OBJECT dynsym + R_*_COPY; ld-linux copies libc's object in at startup). NOT pe/macho at c84: their data-import binding models had not landed. ★ c117 (D-LK-EXTERN-DATA-IMPORT, the got-indirect half): MACHO NOW LANDS — Darwin `#define stdout __stdoutp` (a true extern DATA symbol, no accessor), so macho ships __stdinp/__stdoutp/__stderrp as `kind:object` [macho] (C-name __stdoutp → Mach-O export ___stdoutp) + a macho `macros` variant rewriting stdin/stdout/stderr → __stdinp/__stdoutp/__stderrp (mirrors the pe __iob_func macro). They bind via Mach-O __got non-lazy pointers (macho.format.json dataImportBinding:got-indirect; macho.cpp binds symbolVa[dataExtern] to the __got slot; MIR→LIR lea-of-slot + deref). PE still routes stdout through an ACCESSOR (its __imp_ data thunk model is unbuilt); a pe reference to stdout stays the accessor macro, not a data object. ★ c85 (shell.c `setvbuf(stderr, 0, _IONBF, 0)`): the setvbuf MODE DOMAIN ships complete (_IOFBF/_IOLBF/_IONBF — the SEEK_*/F_OK closed-domain precedent; setvbuf itself shipped at c82). VALUES DIVERGE per-format: glibc stdio.h 0/1/2 (verified /usr/include/stdio.h:94-96) = Darwin (BSD lineage 0/1/2) but msvcrt 0x0000/0x0040/0x0004 → _IOFBF stays FLAT (0 everywhere, the errno low-block discipline); _IOLBF/_IONBF carry per-format `variants` (the FILENAME_MAX mechanism). | ★ P3 COMPLETE (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION §7c, TF-C111 — `library.pe` above is now `ucrtbase.dll`): the WHOLE pe printf/scanf family — `printf`, `fprintf`, `sprintf`, `vfprintf`, `sscanf` — is COMPILER-SYNTHESIZED, not imported. The modern UCRT exports NOT ONE of those five names (MEASURED, `objdump -p C:/Windows/System32/ucrtbase.dll`, against a msvcrt.dll control that exports all five): in a real MSVC build each is a HEADER INLINE over one of the `__stdio_common_v*` cores, so a compiler that binds the CRT by export table finds nothing to import and must supply the body. Each pe row below therefore carries `synthesize: "<name>"` and splits `[elf,macho]` (the real libc import, unchanged) vs `[pe]` (the shim) — the `mtx_lock` precedent in threads.json. The synth pass is src/mir/merge/synth_stdio_shim.cpp; the recipe ids are the loader's closed `kRecipes` vocabulary, and a row here with no arm there (or vice-versa) fails loud rather than silently under-defining a symbol. The earlier increment shipped `sprintf` ALONE, deliberately, because it was the family member with the SMALLEST co-state surface — it formats into a caller-owned buffer, so it creates and consumes no `FILE*`, no CRT fd, and no heap block — and that mattered while pe was running SPLIT-CRT (stdio still msvcrt, the one helper overridden to ucrtbase). ★ THE SPLIT IS NOW RETIRED: the whole co-state group (malloc/stdlib/string/stdio/io/errno/direct/process/sys-stat) flipped in ONE commit, so `fprintf`/`sscanf` — which DO take a `FILE*` and DO write errno — are safe to synthesize too. The two seams the sprintf-only note called out are exactly the ones that closes: `__stdio_common_vsprintf` touches per-CRT state on exactly two of them. (1) **errno** — its parameter-validation paths write ucrtbase's errno; MEASURED: `sprintf(buf, NULL)` returns -1 and sets ucrtbase errno to 22 (EINVAL), which a program reading msvcrt's errno cannot see (a different TLS slot). (2) **the ambient locale** — the shim passes `_Locale = NULL`, i.e. ucrtbase's locale object, so a `setlocale()` routed to msvcrt is invisible to it. Both were inert for every consumer at the time (nothing in the sqlite/tcl tree reads errno after a sprintf, and DSS never calls setlocale; the C locale agrees across both runtimes) — but they were real seams, and the group flip is what closes them: there is now ONE errno and ONE locale on pe. ★ THE FOUR CORES, all ORDINARY pe symbol rows below (user decision — a normal FFI import is a name the eager-import law verifies for us, so the synth pass needs no helper-import machinery and just resolves each by NAME against the module's imports): `__stdio_common_vsprintf` (sprintf), `__stdio_common_vfprintf` (printf/fprintf/vfprintf), `__stdio_common_vsscanf` (sscanf), plus the `__acrt_iob_func` accessor `printf` needs to reach stdout. `_Options` is 1 = `LEGACY_VSPRINTF_NULL_TERMINATION` (bit 0) for `sprintf` ALONE — exactly what a real CRT `sprintf` passes internally — and 0 for the other four (`_CRT_INTERNAL_LOCAL_{PRINTF,SCANF}_OPTIONS` are zero absent the legacy opt-ins `legacy_stdio_definitions.lib` sets, and DSS links no such lib; on the scanf side a nonzero bit 0 would silently turn this into `sscanf_s`, which eats an extra buffer-size argument per `%s`). `sprintf`/`sscanf` pair theirs with `_BufferCount=(size_t)-1`, UCRT's unbounded sentinel (neither has a length limit, unlike snprintf's real count). The TRANSITIONAL per-symbol `library` override the `__stdio_common_vsprintf` row carried is RETIRED here — it existed only because this file's own default was still msvcrt.dll, which does not export that symbol at all, so an un-overridden row would have broken every pe binary's LOAD (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT); with the default now ucrtbase.dll the override is redundant, exactly as `strftime`'s was retired in time.json's P2. Runtime witnesses: `examples/c-subset/shipped_sprintf_ucrt` + `shipped_sprintf_ucrt_crosscu`. Full arc: D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION.
